facts.claim: Arabic 2:255 = Tanzil Uthmani snapshot string (see ayah_text); CC BY 3.0, verbatim only, credit Tanzil Project + link; PC byte-check vs tanzil.net advisable
Hindi = saral bhaavarth from 3 accepted translations (al-Umari, Mahmud Hasan, Tanzil hi.hindi); no translation text is copied
2:255 in Al-Baqarah (2nd surah), 255th ayah (Kufi count), surah 286 ayat (counters differ: 287), juz 3
Al-Baqarah entirely Madani, no disagreement
Name 'Ayat al-Kursi' used in Sahih al-Bukhari wording (aayat al-kursi)
Ayah has ten complete sentences
Link 2:254 (shafa'a mentioned) -> 2:255 (intercession only by permission): no tafseer source found
No sound specific shan-e-nuzul for 2:255 found; Wahidi dataset has 2:256 but not 2:255; IK/MQ/JAL/Baghawi none
Safe wording: no strong occasion reported; part of Al-Baqarah revealed in Madina
Qurtubi: revealed at night, Zayd called to write it (no isnad)
Ibn Abi Hatim 2580 (Ibn Abbas): Musa AS, two bottles, 'then Ayat al-Kursi was revealed' - Israelite-style; Qurtubi: similar report not sahih
Rabi' bin Anas: kursi verse revealed, companions ask about Arsh, 39:67 revealed - mursal tabi'i, other ayah
Ibn al-Hanafiyya: idols/crowns fell, devils fled - no isnad
Tabari's own context for the intercession line (polytheists' idol-worship) - not a chained shan-e-nuzul; do not call it that
Tirmidhi 2878 'sayyid al-ayat' - daif (Shakir, Albani, Bashar, Zubair)
Tirmidhi 2879 Ha-Mim al-Mu'min + Ayat al-Kursi morning/evening - daif (Shakir, Albani, Zubair); Tirmidhi: gharib
Tirmidhi 2880 Abu Ayyub ghoul - ikhtilaaf (Shakir/Albani sahih, Zubair daif; Tirmidhi hasan gharib); jinn content
Greatest Name in 2:255 and 3:1-2 (Asma bint Yazid) - out of video scope; IK: Tirmidhi hasan sahih
Ayah has tongue and two lips at the leg of the Throne (Ahmad) - grade not checked; Muslim omits it
50 words x 50 blessings; a third of the Quran; 'Wali-ullah' in Torah - no isnad/grade
Hadith qudsi to Musa: reward of prophets for each prayer (via al-Hakim al-Tirmidhi) - no grade
Kursi a pearl, qalam a pearl (Ali, Ibn Asakir) - no grade
Umar / companion wrestles jinn (Darimi, Abu Nu'aym) - jinn narrative, no second grader
Ali / Anas versions of the after-prayer reward - weak (second-hand summary)
Tirmidhi 2884 Ibn Mas'ud - one grader only, mauquf
La ilaha illa Huwa: none worthy of worship but Him
Al-Hayy al-Qayyum: ever-living, sustains all, needs none
Sinah/nawm: no drowsiness, no sleep; no shortcoming/heedlessness
Everything in heavens and earth is His
No intercession except by His permission
He knows what is before and behind them (both readings allowed)
None encompass any of His knowledge except what He wills
His Kursi extends over heavens and earth (reality of Kursi: see K1-K6)
Their preservation does not burden/tire Him
Al-'Aliyy al-'Azim: most high in rank, most great
Kursi = His knowledge (Ibn Abbas via Sa'id ibn Jubayr); Tabari prefers
Kursi = a great creation before the Arsh ('place of the feet' wording, Ibn Abbas mauquf, Hakim sahih; Abu Musa munqati'); Qurtubi: most reports point here
Seven heavens in the Kursi like a ring thrown in a desert; Arsh over Kursi likewise (Abu Dharr)
facts.note: Qurtubi: Ajurri, Ibn Hibban in his Sahih, Bayhaqi said sahih; Albani Silsila Sahiha 109 per secondary only

facts.claim: Hasan: Kursi = Arsh itself
Kursi is not a seat for Allah to sit on; He is above sitting/standing/place; Salaf: accept as it came without likening
Some translations render Kursi as sovereignty (hi.farooq 'prabhuta', Maududi 'hukumat'); others literal
Greatest ayah: Sahih Muslim 810 (Ubayy bin Ka'b) - exact Arabic in ayah_text/hadith_text; supported by Ahmad (IK/MQ) and Qurtubi
facts.hadith_arabic: يَا أَبَا الْمُنْذِرِ أَتَدْرِي أَىُّ آيَةٍ مِنْ كِتَابِ اللَّهِ مَعَكَ أَعْظَمُ ... قَالَ قُلْتُ اللَّهُ لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ هُوَ الْحَىُّ الْقَيُّومُ ... وَقَالَ وَاللَّهِ لِيَهْنِكَ الْعِلْمُ أَبَا الْمُنْذِرِ
facts.hadith_english_dataset: O Abu'l-Mundhir, do you know the verse from the Book of Allah which, according to you, is the greatest? ... I said: Allah, there is no god but He, the Living, the Eternal. Thereupon he struck me on my breast and said: May knowledge be pleasant for you, O Abu'l-Mundhir

facts.claim: Bedtime: recite Ayat al-Kursi -> a guard from Allah stays, Shaytan will not come near till morning (Abu Hurayrah) - Bukhari 2311 (full), 3275, 5010; Nasa'i 'Amal al-Yawm per Ibn Kathir
